The Opportunity

A generation is learning about money from TikTok and costly mistakes.

75% of American teens lack basic financial literacy. Only 23 states require personal finance in high schools. Parents want to teach their kids but don't know how.

The result: kids enter adulthood without understanding credit, investing, taxes, or budgeting. They learn from social media, trial-and-error, or not at all — and the mistakes are expensive.

Why now: AI makes personalized, scalable education possible for the first time. Gen Alpha is digital-native. Post-COVID schools need modern digital curriculum. And financial literacy is having a legislative and cultural moment.

Our Solution

Meet kids where they are — on their phones — with an AI companion that makes money approachable.

Think Duolingo meets Khan Academy, but conversational, AI-powered, and built specifically for financial literacy.

AI Conversations

Kids chat with MoneyBot to learn saving, investing, budgeting, and earning. The AI adapts to each child's age, knowledge level, and interests.

Real-World Simulations

Practice with virtual money before touching real accounts. Kids build confidence through doing — from budgeting an allowance to understanding credit.

Parent Dashboard

Parents track progress, set goals, and unlock real-world challenges tied to allowance — turning lessons into habits at home.

Traction

Launched January 2026. Four months later, traction is generating its own word of mouth.

We reached 10 schools and 200+ weekly active users with zero marketing spend. Local news stations in Louisville and Lexington reached out to cover the story — not the other way around.

Market

A $40M+ ARR opportunity domestically — before we leave the US.

50 million kids aged 8–16 in the US. Capturing just 1% at $80/year ARPU equals a $40M ARR opportunity domestically.

The B2B school market alone is an $8B+ annual spend on curriculum, tools, and professional development. Schools are desperate for modern financial literacy solutions that actually engage students.

Competitive landscape: Greenlight, GoHenry, and FamZoo focus on spending controls, not education. Khan Academy and YouTube are passive and one-size-fits-all. MoneyBot owns the learning layer.
